findings.title: Remove the previous local code set when storing a replacement externally
findings.body: When a federated user already has locally stored recovery codes—the creation path used before this change—a successful external update leaves that local credential untouched. Credential validation can fall back to the local recovery-code provider when the external validator rejects an input, so codes from the previous set remain valid after the user generates a replacement externally. Remove existing local recovery-code credentials as part of a successful external replacement, and test this migration scenario.

findings.title: Export OTP credentials with the canonical OTP type
findings.body: The new getCredentials override returns the stored OTP model unchanged, but updateCredential sets that model's type from the registration input. CredentialHelper supplies the realm policy type, 'totp' or 'hotp', whereas OTP credential providers and account credential listings use the canonical type 'otp'. Consequently, the exported credential does not match the OTP listing, breaking the existing account-listing/removal behavior. Return an OTP-typed representation rather than exposing the legacy validation record unchanged.

findings.title: The federation fixture never consumes validated recovery codes
findings.body: Recovery-code validation only checks membership in the saved list and never records consumption. Since getCredentials reconstructs a credential from that unchanged list, the requested code remains code 0, previously used codes remain valid indefinitely, and allCodesUsed() never becomes true. The new test performs only one login, so it cannot exercise advancement, replay rejection, or the exhausted-federated-credential branch changed by this PR. Maintain consumption and next-code state in the fixture and extend the test to cover repeated login and exhaustion.
